page_shape.job_page: linkedin.com/jobs/view/<id>/ with a top-card button 'Easy Apply' (aria-label 'Easy Apply to this job') and 'Save'. Authenticated session required to see the button state; no sign-in wall was shown because the profile was logged in.
page_shape.modal: Clicking Easy Apply appends ?companyName=…&trackingId=…&applicantTrackingSystemName=LinkedIn to the URL and opens a native <dialog> element (NOT role=dialog). Header 'Apply to <company>', a page counter 'N/M pages', a step title, controls, and footer buttons Dismiss / Next (Back appears on later pages, unverified).
page_shape.draft_prompt: Dismiss on a started application opens a second <dialog> 'Save this application? … Any uploaded files will not be saved.' with buttons Discard / Save.

control_families.select: native <select> with label '<text>*' (required marker is a trailing '*' in the label). Email address select lists the account's verified emails (1 option, PRIVATE). Phone country code select has 249 options 'Country (+code)'.
control_families.tel: input[type=tel] 'Mobile phone number*' prefilled from profile (PRIVATE).
control_families.text: input[type=text] for First name / Last name / Address / City / State / Postal when the employer requests full contact details (li-03).

blockers.detail: LinkedIn login required for Easy Apply; session was already authenticated, no challenge shown
Page 1 is prefilled with account email/phone/name/location. Runtime must never export or send these values to models; observation should emit labels and has_value flags only.
Pressing Next persists an application draft on LinkedIn; abandoning triggers a Save/Discard prompt

runtime_observations: Modal detection must include the native <dialog> tag; role=dialog matching alone misses it.
Two <dialog> elements can be open at once (application + Save prompt); pick the last visible one.
Step title text can be localised (Kontaktinfo) even when field labels are English; do not key on step title strings.
Element ids use React useId style («r6») and are unstable; OpenCLI refs re-numbered after the modal opened (Easy Apply button became ref 1).
Email is a select over account emails: the runtime cannot enter an arbitrary verified email; it must match the candidate's email to an option or escalate.

typical_stages_unverified: Easy Apply modal page 1 Contact info
inferred.page_count_inference: 'N pages' likely equals number of steps including Review; employer screening questions add pages.
inferred.screening_question_inference: LinkedIn screening questions are typically numeric (years of experience), yes/no, or single-select with employer 'ideal answer' filtering; free-text is rare.

provider_hint.for_jev: LinkedIn Easy Apply is a multi-page <dialog>. Page 1 = contact info prefilled from the account (private; labels only). Required = label ends with '*'. Email is a select over account emails. Later pages unobserved: expect resume choice, employer screening questions, review. Never press Next in prepare-only mode unless root authorises draft creation; never press Submit application.
option_choice_from_verified_facts: email (must match an account email option)
escalate_to_writer_opus: none observed on page 1; later-page free-text questions if any
requires_human_input: confirmation before any Next press (draft persistence)
